related_advisory: https://spring.io/security/cve-2024-22243/ (CVE-2024-22243, 1st of the family); https://spring.io/security/cve-2024-22259/ (CVE-2024-22259, 2nd of the family / this case's V1 seed)
incomplete_fix_quote: Applications that use UriComponentsBuilder to parse an externally provided URL (e.g. through a query parameter) AND perform validation checks on the host of the parsed URL may be vulnerable to open redirect or SSRF. This is the same as CVE-2024-22243 and CVE-2024-22259, but with different input. The CVE-2024-22259 fix (6.1.5) made USERINFO accept '@' and HOST_IPV4 accept '[' and added checkSchemeAndHost, but left the backslash '\' out of the excluded character classes, so a URL using '\' still makes getHost() report the allow-listed host while a browser navigates elsewhere.
root_cause: org.springframework.web.util.UriComponentsBuilder parses the authority with a regex whose SCHEME/USERINFO/HOST/PORT character classes disagree with the WHATWG (browser/fetch) host algorithm. A browser treats backslash '\' as '/' in special (http/https) schemes and ends the authority at the first '\'. Spring 6.1.5's regex still ALLOWS '\' inside USERINFO and HOST_IPV4, and '(userinfo@)?' binds to the LAST '@', so for 'http://attacker\@allowlisted' Spring reports host=allowlisted (used by an app allow-list guard) while the real navigation target is 'attacker'. CVE-2024-22262 (6.1.6) adds '\' to the excluded sets of SCHEME/USERINFO/HOST_IPV4/PORT, aligning the authority boundary with the browser.
distinctness_vs_cve_2024_22259: GENUINELY DISTINCT residual. CVE-2024-22259 = 'http://@trusted.internal[@sidecar.internal': allow-listed host FIRST, attacker LAST; abuses a LEADING '@' + HOST_IPV4 truncation at '[' (both '[' and leading '@' matter). CVE-2024-22262 = 'http://sidecar.internal\@trusted.internal': attacker host FIRST, allow-listed host LAST; abuses BACKSLASH '\' (WHATWG '\'->'/' authority terminator) with Spring's last-'@' userinfo binding. Different character ('\' vs '['), different browser mechanism, opposite host ordering. Confirmed at runtime: on V1=6.1.5 the -22259 seed is BLOCKED (getHost=sidecar.internal) whereas the -22262 residual PASSES (getHost=trusted.internal) -- so they are not the same residual.

versions.v0_vulnerable: 6.1.4 (CVE-2024-22243 fix; still vulnerable to CVE-2024-22259: USERINFO '([^@/?#]*)' excludes '@', HOST_IPV4 '[^\[/?#:]*' excludes '[')
versions.v1_incomplete: 6.1.5 (CVE-2024-22259 fix: USERINFO '([^/?#]*)', HOST_IPV4 '[^/?#:]*', checkSchemeAndHost; the target -- backslash '\' still allowed)

diff_v1_to_v2: SCHEME_PATTERN '([^:/?#]+):' -> '([^:/?#\\]+):'; USERINFO_PATTERN '([^/?#]*)' -> '([^/?#\\]*)'; HOST_IPV4_PATTERN '[^/?#:]*' -> '[^/?#:\\]*'; PORT_PATTERN '(\{[^}]+\}?|[^/?#]*)' -> '(\{[^}]+\}?|[^/?#\\]*)'. (Only these four char-class edits touch the getHost() parse; the rest of the 6.1.5->6.1.6 diff is unrelated @Nullable annotations.)

reference_witnesses.original_cve_2024_22259: url 'http://@trusted.internal[@sidecar.internal' -> Spring getHost()=trusted.internal on V0=6.1.4 (guard passes); browser/WHATWG host=sidecar.internal. getHost()=sidecar.internal on V1=6.1.5 -> blocked.
reference_witnesses.bypass_cve_2024_22262: url 'http://sidecar.internal\@trusted.internal' -> Spring getHost()=trusted.internal on V0=6.1.4 and V1=6.1.5 (guard passes); browser/WHATWG host=sidecar.internal. getHost()=sidecar.internal on V2=6.1.6 -> blocked.
